newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says German firms sued for Iraq chemical help.
newsitem.headline: Iran says German firms sued for Iraq chemical help.

text.p: Court proceedings will begin shortly against 24 German companies reported to have helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during its 1980-88 war with Iran, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.

Deputy judiciary chief Mohammad Reza Abbasi-Fard, quoted by IRNA, said the complaints against the companies had been lodged by more than 1,000 relatives of Iranians killed or wounded as a result of Iraq's use of banned chemical weapons during the war.
He did not say when or where the trial would be held or which companies were involved. He also did not give further details on the proceedings.

Germany said on Monday it was ready to review its relations with Iran, depending on Tehran's reaction when a Berlin court rules this week in the trial of men accused of killing Kurdish opposition leaders on Iran's orders.

Iran has repeatedly expressed its anger with the German prosecutors who have accused Iran of "state terrorism" and issued an arrest warrant for Iran's intelligence minister, Ali Fallahiyan, in connection with the killings.

"Abbasi-Fard said that the group has called for legal action against those responsible for the supply of the chemical weapons and lethal gases and substances to Iraq which were deployed against the Iranian forces," IRNA said. "They have also demanded payment of reparations."
He said the relatives had also called for the punishment of German officials who had allegedly issued licences for the export of the substances, IRNA reported.

"The spokesman added that there are undeniable documents including pictures, films and recorded remarks of the German experts while cooperating with (the) Iraqi army, adding that the culprits should attend court shortly to defend themselves," the agency said.
Iran had as far back as 1987 accused West German companies of helping Iraq produce internationally banned chemical weapons.
